document.title: Talking Points (undated, likely November 1998)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan's Bin Laden Policy
document.note: [Secret/NODIS] State Department talking points say the U.S. has pressed the Taliban directly and through Pakistan to expel bin Laden, without success. The issue is to be raised at the December 2, 1998 Clinton-Sharif meeting. The Taliban will not surrender him, partly because of his close ties to Mullah Omar, and Pakistan has not been supportive. The time for a diplomatic solution may be running out. Excised.

events.description: Planned meeting of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif with the US President, seen as an opportunity to press the Bin Laden message.
US exerted diplomatic pressure on the Taliban, directly and through Pakistan, to expel Bin Laden; unsuccessful so far.
US indictment of Bin Laden was brushed off by the Taliban.

The Taliban gave the U.S. their word they would prevent terrorism from Afghan soil but broke the promise.
The Taliban brushed off the U.S. indictment of Bin Ladin and other evidence.

key_claims: The Taliban promised to prevent terrorism from Afghan soil but broke that promise.
The Taliban provide sanctuary to Bin Laden and his network.
The US pressed the Taliban directly and via Pakistan to expel Bin Laden, without success.
Bin Laden's close ties to Mullah Omar and other key leaders preserve his position despite Taliban divisions.
The Taliban's desire for international contact gives the US leverage.
The Taliban's brush-off of the indictment may signal a shift from tolerance to more active support of Bin Laden.
